titanic.voice.n001.text: [cheerfully] Alright? I'm Alfie, a stoker. I'm feeding this furnace, and believe me, she eats more than my whole family put together!

titanic.voice.n002.text: [brightly] Hello! I'm Jimmy, a stoker. This is my very first voyage, and I've already got coal dust in places I didn't know I had!

titanic.voice.n003.text: [warmly] Evening! I'm Fred, a stoker. I'm keeping an eye on the steam gauge. When that needle climbs, we're doing our job right.

titanic.voice.n004.text: [playfully] Watch your step! I'm Charlie, a trimmer. I wheel the coal from the bunkers to the furnaces. I must have pushed this barrow halfway to New York already!

titanic.voice.n005.text: [cheerfully] Hello there! I'm Billy, a stoker. I'm on the four-to-eight watch, and I'm counting the shovels till supper. Only about three thousand to go!

titanic.voice.n006.text: [friendly] Hiya! I'm Sam, a stoker. I'm cleaning out the ash from this fire. Tidy fires burn the brightest, my old dad always said.

titanic.voice.n007.text: [enthusiastic] Hello! I'm Ted, a stoker. I'm on my break, sort of. I'm teaching Sam a new song to shovel to. It helps keep the rhythm!

titanic.voice.n008.text: [proudly] Hello! I'm Harry, a stoker. I've been at sea for ten years, and this is the finest boiler room I've ever worked in.

titanic.voice.n009.text: [cheerfully] Ey up! I'm Joe, a stoker. I'm checking the fire bars, and keeping my eyebrows well away from the flames!

titanic.voice.n010.text: [warmly] Hello, young explorer! I'm Ned, a stoker. I'm the oldest fellow down here, so the lads call me Grandad. I don't mind one bit.

titanic.voice.n011.text: [brightly] Alright! I'm Davy, a stoker. I'm opening the furnace door just a crack. Ooh, feel that warm glow!

titanic.voice.n012.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Bert, a greaser. I oil the giant engines, so everything runs smooth as butter. I go through buckets of oil!

titanic.voice.n013.text: [excited] Hello there! I'm Tommy, a greaser too. I'm listening to the engines. When they hum just right, it sounds like music to me!

titanic.voice.n014.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Jack, a stoker. I'm heading down to start my watch. This long passage is called Scotland Road, and we walk it every day.

titanic.voice.n015.text: [warmly] Hiya! I'm Walter, a stoker. I've just finished my watch, and I'm off for a wash and a big plate of stew!

titanic.voice.n020.text: [warmly, a little grand] Good evening! I'm Percy, head steward of the dining saloon. I'm checking every table is perfect before the bugle calls for dinner.

titanic.voice.n021.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Wilfred, a dining saloon steward. I'm folding napkins into little swans. This is my two hundredth one today!

titanic.voice.n022.text: [friendly] Good evening! I'm Cyril, a steward. I'm laying out the silver, and I'm making sure every spoon can see its own reflection.

titanic.voice.n023.text: [warmly] Hello, dear! I'm Mabel, a stewardess. I'm waiting here at the Grand Staircase to help passengers find their way to dinner.

titanic.voice.n024.text: [politely] Good evening! I'm Herbert, a steward in the Reception Room. I'm keeping the band's sheet music in order. It blew all over the place this morning!

titanic.voice.n025.text: [calmly] Hello there! I'm Stanley, a bath steward. I'm warming the towels for the Turkish bath. Toasty towels are the secret of a happy passenger.

titanic.voice.n026.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Leonard, the swimming bath steward. I'm checking the water. It's seawater, so don't be surprised if it tastes salty!

titanic.voice.n027.text: [brightly] Going down? I'm Albert, a steward, and I run one of the lifts. Up and down, all day long. I'm the only person on board who goes everywhere!

titanic.voice.n028.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Edith, a stewardess. I'm taking a breakfast tray up to a lady who loves her toast extra crispy. Very, very crispy!

titanic.voice.n029.text: [warmly] Hello! I'm Florence, but everyone calls me Flo. I'm a stewardess, and I'm tidying the Reading and Writing Room. People write so many postcards!

titanic.voice.n030.text: [softly cheerful] Hello! I'm Winifred, a stewardess. I'm sharpening pencils for the writing desks. I've done forty this morning, and I've only snapped two!

titanic.voice.n031.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Ada, a stewardess. I look after twenty cabins on B deck, and I know every passenger's favourite kind of tea.

titanic.voice.n032.text: [brightly] Hello! I'm Lily, a stewardess. I'm carrying fresh flowers to the parlour suites. These roses came all the way from Southampton!

titanic.voice.n033.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Elsie, a stewardess. I'm turning down the beds for tonight. I fold every sheet into a perfect triangle. Forty beds, forty triangles!

titanic.voice.n034.text: [warmly] Hello there! I'm Rose, a stewardess. I'm mending a button on a gentleman's coat. My needle and thread go everywhere with me.

titanic.voice.n035.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Nellie, a second-class stewardess. I'm bringing hot water bottles round. The Atlantic gets chilly at night!

titanic.voice.n036.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Ivy, a stewardess. I'm helping a family find their cabin. These corridors are long, so I always say, follow the numbers!

titanic.voice.n037.text: [cheerfully] Good evening! I'm Reginald, a second-class saloon steward. Tonight it's roast turkey, and I've already had a sneaky sniff of the gravy!

titanic.voice.n038.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Frank, a steward. I'm counting the chairs in the second-class saloon. Three hundred and ninety-four. Every time!

titanic.voice.n039.text: [politely] Good evening! I'm Edwin, a waiter in the à la carte restaurant. I'm polishing the glasses until they sparkle like stars.

titanic.voice.n040.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Arthur, a waiter. I'm learning the French names on tonight's menu. Pommes de terre... that just means potatoes!

titanic.voice.n041.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Bertie, a steward in the barber's shop. I'm sweeping up the hair. This morning I swept up enough for a whole new moustache!

titanic.voice.n042.text: [warmly] Hello! I'm Daisy, a third-class stewardess. I'm helping with the sing-song tonight. Somebody brought a fiddle, and somebody brought bagpipes!

titanic.voice.n043.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Harold, a third-class steward. I'm handing out programmes for tonight's music. Everybody's welcome!

titanic.voice.n050.text: [warmly] Hello there! I'm Michael, an able seaman. I'm checking the anchor chains are snug. Each link of that chain is as heavy as a grown man!

titanic.voice.n051.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Thomas, a seaman. I'm coiling ropes on the forecastle. A tidy rope is a happy rope, my granny used to say!

titanic.voice.n052.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Francis, a seaman. I'm greasing the capstans so the anchors come up nice and smooth.

titanic.voice.n053.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Peter, a seaman. I work the cargo crane in this well deck. Back in Southampton, I lifted a whole motor car on board! Very carefully.

titanic.voice.n054.text: [warmly] Hello! I'm Daniel, a seaman. I'm painting the railings. It's my favourite job, because you can see the sea the whole time.

titanic.voice.n055.text: [friendly] Hello! I'm Joseph, a seaman. I'm polishing the brass on the bridge deck. If the sun catches it right, you can see it from a mile away!

titanic.voice.n056.text: [cheerfully] Hello there! I'm Liam, a seaman. I'm scrubbing the boat deck. We scrub it every morning with sand and seawater. It's called holystoning!

titanic.voice.n057.text: [warmly] Hello! I'm James, a seaman. I'm checking the ropes on the boat deck. I learned all my knots from my father, back home in Ireland.

titanic.voice.n058.text: [brightly] Hello! I'm Kieran, a seaman. I'm on lookout for whales and dolphins. Keep your eyes open, you never know what might pop up!

titanic.voice.n059.text: [cheerfully] Hello! I'm Conor, a seaman. I'm raising the flag at the stern. The White Star flag, with its red swallowtail. Isn't she grand?

titanic.voice.n060.text: [warmly] Hello there! I'm Seán, a seaman. I joined the ship at Queenstown, so I've only been aboard a little while, and I'm still finding my way around!

titanic.voice.steward.l00.text: [curiously] Did you know? [proudly] This ship is two hundred and sixty-nine metres long. That's longer than two and a half football pitches, end to end!

titanic.voice.steward.l01.text: [proudly] Here's something remarkable. The first-class dining saloon seats almost six hundred people at once. [amused] That is a LOT of soup to carry.

titanic.voice.steward.l02.text: [curiously] Did you know? We loaded forty thousand fresh eggs before we sailed. Scrambled, fried, boiled... [cheerfully] we are ready for anything!

titanic.voice.steward.l03.text: [proudly] Here's something remarkable. Our pantries hold forty-four thousand pieces of cutlery. [sighs dramatically] And yes, every single fork has to be polished.

titanic.voice.steward.l04.text: [curiously] Did you know? We brought twelve hundred quarts of ice cream on board. [conspiratorially] Pudding is taken very seriously on this ship.

titanic.voice.steward.l05.text: [proudly] Here's something remarkable. There are three passenger lifts beside the Grand Staircase for first class, and one for second class. Lifts! On a ship! [excited] The very latest thing.

titanic.voice.steward.l12.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke for you! Why did the cookie go to see the ship's doctor?... Because it was feeling crummy!

titanic.voice.steward.l13.text: [chuckling] Oh, here's one that always gets a laugh! Why did the tomato blush at dinner?... Because it saw the salad dressing!

titanic.voice.steward.l14.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke for you! What do sea monsters like best for dinner?... Fish and ships!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l00.text: [brightly] Did you know? Our Grand Staircase runs from the boat deck down to D deck, under a glass dome. [dreamily] When the sun shines through, it sparkles like a jewel box.

titanic.voice.stewardess.l01.text: [warmly] Ooh, here's a lovely fact! At the top of the Grand Staircase there's a carved clock called Honour and Glory Crowning Time. [laughs softly] And still everybody asks me what time it is!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l02.text: [brightly] Did you know? At the foot of the staircase stands a little bronze cherub holding up a lamp. [warmly] The children always give him a wave.

titanic.voice.stewardess.l03.text: [warmly] Ooh, here's a lovely fact! First class has four grand parlour suites, each with a sitting room, two bedrooms and a private bathroom. [impressed] Fancy that!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l04.text: [brightly] Did you know? There are a hundred and seven children on this voyage. [cheerfully] So if you hear giggling in the corridors, now you know why!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l05.text: [warmly] Ooh, here's a lovely fact! This ship can carry over three and a half thousand people, passengers and crew together. [amazed] A whole town, floating on the sea.

titanic.voice.stewardess.l06.text: [brightly] Did you know? First class even has kennels for the passengers' dogs, up on the boat deck. [playfully] Some of those dogs are better travelled than I am!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l13.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke! Why did the teddy bear say no to pudding?... Because he was already stuffed!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l14.text: [giggling] Would you like a joke? Here goes! What's the most musical part of a fish?... The scales!

titanic.voice.stewardess.l15.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke! Why are fish so clever?... Because they live in schools!

titanic.voice.stoker.l00.text: [excited] Did you know? Down here we've got twenty-nine boilers with a hundred and fifty-nine furnaces. [excited] And every single one of them is hungry for coal!

titanic.voice.stoker.l01.text: [cheerfully] Here's a fact for you! This ship burns more than six hundred tonnes of coal a day. [amazed] That's about as heavy as a hundred elephants!

titanic.voice.stoker.l02.text: [excited] Did you know? We work in shifts called watches. Four hours on, eight hours off, [cheerfully] then back to the shovel!

titanic.voice.stoker.l03.text: [cheerfully] Here's a fact for you! Each of these boilers is nearly five metres across and weighs over ninety tonnes. [impressed] That's heavier than fifteen elephants. Each!

titanic.voice.stoker.l04.text: [excited] Did you know? We clear away about a hundred tonnes of ash every single day. [laughs] Sweeping up after these fires is a big job!

titanic.voice.stoker.l05.text: [cheerfully] Here's a fact for you! There are a hundred and seventy-six of us firemen keeping the fires going, [proudly] all day and all night.

titanic.voice.stoker.l06.text: [excited] Did you know? The trimmers fetch coal from the bunkers in their barrows, so we stokers never run out. [warmly] Teamwork, that is.

titanic.voice.stoker.l13.text: [grinning] I've got a funny joke! Why did the scarecrow win a prize? Because he was outstanding in his field! [proudly] Me, I'm outstanding in my boiler room.

titanic.voice.stoker.l14.text: [cheekily] Want to hear a joke? Here's one! What do you call a pig that does karate?... A pork chop!

titanic.voice.stoker.l15.text: [grinning] I've got a funny joke! Why did the man keep his money in the freezer? He wanted cold, hard cash! [laughs] No chance of freezing anything down here, it's toasty.

titanic.voice.seaman.l00.text: [warmly] Did you know? This ship was built in Belfast, at the Harland and Wolff shipyard. [proudly] About fifteen thousand men worked in that yard!

titanic.voice.seaman.l01.text: [proudly] Now, here's a grand fact for you. When she was launched, they greased the slipway with twenty-two tonnes of soap and tallow. [excited] She slid into the water in just sixty-two seconds!

titanic.voice.seaman.l02.text: [warmly] Did you know? A hundred thousand people came to watch her launch, back in May nineteen eleven. [amazed] Biggest crowd I ever saw.

titanic.voice.seaman.l03.text: [proudly] Now, here's a grand fact for you. Her hull is held together by more than three million rivets. [laughs] Somebody had to hammer in every single one!

titanic.voice.seaman.l04.text: [warmly] Did you know? Our centre anchor weighs about sixteen tonnes. It took twenty big Clydesdale horses to pull it to the railway station!

titanic.voice.seaman.l05.text: [proudly] Now, here's a grand fact for you. The rudder is twenty-four metres tall and weighs over a hundred tonnes. [impressed] Like a door the size of a building!

titanic.voice.seaman.l06.text: [warmly] Did you know? These funnels are so wide, you could drive a railway train right through one!

titanic.voice.seaman.l13.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke for you! Why are pirates called pirates?... Because they arrrrr!

titanic.voice.seaman.l14.text: [chuckling] Here's one my granny used to tell! What do you call a fish with no eyes?... A fsh!

titanic.voice.seaman.l15.text: [playfully] I have a funny joke for you! What's the best way to talk to a fish?... Drop it a line!
